observed.reply:
It makes sense that the word feels awkward: “designer” names a role you’ve inhabited for a while, while “manager” may still feel like a responsibility you’re learning to claim. Liking the new work and feeling hesitant about the title can both be true; you don’t have to force the label to feel fully natural before using it.

You could try an introduction that names the transition honestly:

- “Hi, I’m [Name]. I’ve worked as a designer, and I’m now managing the team.”
- “I’m [Name], the team’s new manager—I’m coming into the role from a design background.”
- “I’m [Name]. I lead this team, after several years working as a designer.”

The first may fit if you want to honor where you came from; the second is straightforward and low-drama; the third emphasizes what you do now without pretending the old identity disappeared. Which part feels most important to keep visible: your design background, your new responsibility, or the fact that you’re still growing into both?
